text.p: Berner Allgemeine Holding AG, the Swiss insurer, said its Swiss-based premium income in the first nine months of 1996 rose 5.2 percent versus the previous year.

In its nine-month earnings report, it said that the increase, which included business of its three operating companies, Berner Insurance, Berner Life, and Alba, a general insurer based in Basle, reflected mainly one-time contributions to the single premium business in the life sector.
Premiums in the life sector were up by 19.2 percent.
Investment income was up 3.4 percent versus 1995.
The gain was tied mostly to the favourable performance of securities markets. "In total, the financial results in the current year should be slightly better than in 1995," Berner said.
In the non-life business, premium income fell by 3.3 percent. Berner said the decline took into account a deregulation in the car insurance market.
Other factors included a reductions in individual health insurance, as well as declines in branches affected by wages, reflecting the general state of the economy.
It said that non-consolidated capital investments rose in the first nine months by 5.6 percent to 3.6 billion francs.
It said that investments flowed mainly into securities. Real estate investments also rose due to building of a new office in Berne.
Berner reported in June that consolidated net profit for all of 1995 was 18.5 million Swiss francs compared with 16.9 million in 1994.
Berner is 51.0-percent owned by Germany's Allianz AG insurance group.
